---
title: "How this was built"
description: "A human directing AI agents, with the direction kept as an auditable record."
---

Tributary is two projects sharing one repository. The data science build is
the visible one. The primary one is the working method: demonstrating that a
human can direct AI agents to produce real, reviewable work — and keeping
enough of a record that an outside evaluator can decompose who contributed
what. The build is the demonstration payload; the method is the exhibit.

That record is not this page's summary of itself — it is in the repository,
in [meta/](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/tree/main/meta), and it
is the part of the project I would most want an evaluator to open.

## The harness

Agents in this repo do not start from a blank prompt. They start from a
harness built to make them more effective than out-of-the-box:

- **A charter and standing instruction set** —
  [twelve working agreements](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/meta/conventions.md)
  fixed at the start (quality over development cost, no invented company
  names, honesty over flash, comment the code, index the repo for agents)
  plus a mandatory trigger table: *this* event requires *that* record, every
  session.
- **A knowledge graph** —
  [a machine-readable index](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/meta/graph/graph.yaml)
  of every document, package, silo, phase, and decision, validated in CI on
  every push. Agents load it at session start and navigate the repo cheaply
  instead of re-discovering it.
- **A design document as the seed** — the
  [full build design](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/docs/design.md)
  was written first and is kept alive: every change to it cites the decision
  or intervention that caused it, in its changelog.

## The records

- **Decision log** —
  [an ADR series](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/meta/logs/decisions.md)
  for every choice between real alternatives, from cloud naming to why the
  auction linkage is deterministic SQL while the dedupe is probabilistic.
  Agents propose; the human ratifies, amends, or rejects — and the log says
  which happened.
- **Intervention log** —
  [agent errors and the corrections that fixed them](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/meta/logs/interventions.md),
  classified. Kept deliberately: a record of only successes would be
  advertising, not evidence.
- **Prompt log** — the prompts that materially shaped artifacts, recorded
  verbatim minus marked redactions.
- **Per-commit provenance** — every commit carries a trailer classifying its
  content: `H` (human-authored), `HD` (human-directed), `A` (agent-executed),
  per the [provenance spec](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/meta/provenance.md).
  `git log` itself is the contribution ledger.

## The discipline that makes it real

A phase is not done when the code works. It is done when the logs are
current, the graph validates, and provenance is recorded — that global exit
criterion gates every phase alongside its technical one. Several phases
closed only after a ratification round in which proposed decisions were
accepted, amended, or sent back.

Two working rules worth naming because they are easy to fake and expensive to
keep: numbers over adjectives (the ER band was *tuned down* to 0.8–0.9 when
early versions were suspiciously clean, and the uplift experiment is reported
as underpowered because it is), and fictionalization without fictional names
(the simulated marketplace resembles the real world's mechanics but names no
company and reuses no proprietary numbers — every statistic traces to a
public dataset or a declared assumption).
